sentence: POST or PUT /api/journal with a body starting with a NUL character returns 500 because SQLite length() fails the CHECK constraint and the IntegrityError is unhandled.
evidence: Logged in as the demo user through the API. POST /api/journal {"entry_on":"2025-01-01","body":"\u0000x","plant_id":1} returned 'Internal Server Error' [500]. PUT /api/journal/5 with body "\u0000abc" also returned 500. Control cases: 'nul\u0000x' and 'ok' both returned 201. Code check: JournalEntryIn.body only has min_length=1/max_length=500, so Pydantic accepts the value. db.py has CHECK (length(body) BETWEEN 1 AND 500), and SQLite's length() on TEXT stops at the first NUL, so it returns 0 and the INSERT/UPDATE fails. routers/journal.py does not catch sqlite3.IntegrityError, so the client gets an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx validation error. I deleted the test entries afterwards.
